correctness.rationale: Domination in a complete multipartite graph is exactly the condition of meeting at least two parts or being one whole part. A replacement for a selected vertex must lie in a different part. For support at least three, deleting one vertex leaves at least two occupied parts, so the only obstruction is the absence of an outside replacement; for support two and at least three graph parts, an unoccupied third part supplies every replacement. The bipartite boundary is handled separately and yields the stated two implications. The polynomial is obtained by exact inclusion-exclusion from the structural classification. Exhaustive direct checking on every multipartite profile through order ten agrees with both the characterization and polynomial.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches for co-secure domination, cosecure domination, complete multipartite and complete bipartite aliases, all-set classifications, support/complement criteria, and domination polynomials found no covering result. The closest current database result is the secure-domination polynomial of complete multipartite graphs, but secure and co-secure domination reverse the replacement quantifiers and neither all-set classification implies the other. Recent co-secure papers focus on equality characterizations, complexity, jump graphs, and restricted graph classes rather than the complete-multipartite all-set problem.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification for a canonical graph class in an active domination variant, rather than only another upper bound or one small-family value. The structural theorem simultaneously yields the exact minimum, a sharp bipartite boundary including stars, and a closed polynomial enumerating every co-secure dominating set for all multipartite graphs with at least three parts. The reversed secure/co-secure quantifier makes this a distinct feasible-set geometry with reusable counting information.
